section.title: The seam
section.prose: The host-effect seam is the boundary at which the machine offers an effect operation that no source-level handler claims to an ambient host interpreter. It is the earliest bootstrap gate of the native-REPL host handler (ADR-35 D4): a top-level host intercepts a flat effect signature, performs the real operation, and either resumes the delimited continuation with a reply or declines, leaving the machine to take its ordinary step. Its home in the reboot is the host module of crate core-checker.

The seam's whole public vocabulary is three types: a host operation the machine hands out, a host reply the host hands back (resume with a value, or decline), and the host handler that mediates. The machine offers each host-interceptable perform to a host handler; an unclaimed operation the host also declines blames a no-handler outcome under the machine's ordinary step.

section.title: The preserved-boundary property
section.prose: The seam is a preserved boundary : it is expressed only over the public value and effect-signature surface and the operation name, never over a machine continuation frame, so it is representation-independent across whichever evaluator realizes it. That representation-independence is what let the seam survive the port from the retired CEK oracle to its successor: the two machines presented the identical seam to the host. The L machine realization (the run-with-host entry of the core-sequent machine) is the durable driver the host runtime binds against; the CEK drivers retired with the CEK at B1 stage F, and the seam outlived them precisely because the boundary never named a machine's internals.

Because the boundary is preserved, the L machine must present the identical seam the earlier machine did: the host observes the same value and effect-signature surface and the same operation names, and is never exposed to the command IL, the two-region store, or any focused-machine state. The seam is therefore the stable contract between the sole driver, the
, and the headless host-effect runtime.

section.title: Realization and consumers
section.prose: The seam types live in core-checker as a distinct boundary concern, beside the newtype vocabulary and the effect-row algebra. The L machine in core-sequent drives them: it offers each unclaimed perform across the structural prefix and resumes or declines. The headless host-effect runtime, crate runtime-host, is the seam's consumer: it binds a host handler over a flat operation signature, performs the syscall-shaped operation, and resumes with the reply. Keeping the seam machine-independent is what lets that runtime bind once and remain correct across machine and arena changes.
